timeline.title: Board Member (elected)
timeline.description: As a University student I stood for election for the local City Council community board in 2010 to better link students with the wider community. In my 3 year term, I helped our board navigate through a number of complex issues around city planning, infrastructure priorities, disaster response and other community issues. I turned down the opportunity to stand for full council, despite a generous offer to become Deputy Mayor, to pursue opportunities further afield in 2013.

timeline.title: Student Volunteer Army founded

timeline.title: Trustee
timeline.description:

timeline.title: Trustee
timeline.description:
The Plunket Foundation is a stand alone Philanthropic Trust, established by Plunket with generous support from Karitane Products Society (KPS) Limited.

The mandate is simple:

To build an independent, sustainable, world class children’s endowment fund focused on helping New Zealand communities ‘Grow Great Kiwi Kids’ today, tomorrow, and into the future.

A total of 7 prominent New Zealanders*, all passionate about providing children with the best start in life, act as Trustees and sit on the Plunket Foundation Board which is chaired by former New Zealander of the Year, Sir Ray Avery GNZM.

timeline.title: Advisory Trustee
timeline.description:
The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust was established by the New Zealand Government on 23 May 1989. Funding of $3.2 million was received from France in recognition of the events surrounding the destruction of the Greenpeace 'Rainbow Warrior' ship in Auckland Harbour on 10 July 1985.

Every year the Trust has approximately $250,000 to distribute as grants to groups and individuals in the South Pacific for a range of development and conservation projects.

Seven Advisory Trustees are appointed by the Minister having responsibility for disarmament and arms control (as a result of changes in the composition of Ministerial portfolios announced on 12 December 2011, the Minister of Foreign Affairs is now responsible for the responsibilities formerly included in the Disarmament and Arms Control portfolio).

Apply here: http://www.dia.govt.nz/Services-Trust-&-Fellowship-Grants-The-Pacific-Development-and-Conservation-Trust
